brands.logoSvgRefused: SVG cannot be embedded in a PDF by this renderer. Export the logo as PNG \u2014 at about 480 pixels wide it will be sharp on both the page and the print.
brands.textHint: Plain text. Nothing downstream interprets markup, because the PDF writer has no rich-text pipeline.

import.conflictHint: Renaming is the only one of these that cannot lose data.
import.dropHint: Choose one or more kuma.db files
import.dryRunHint: Produces the whole report without writing anything. Worth doing first.
import.filesHint: Usually /app/data/kuma.db inside the Uptime Kuma container. The file is processed and deleted; it is never kept.
import.historyHint: Slower, and much larger. Configuration imports fine without it.
import.intro: Point this at one or more kuma.db files and it reproduces the monitors, tags, notification channels, and status pages. Several files at once merges several Kuma instances into this install.
import.namePrefixHint: Applied to imported monitor names. The practical way to keep several merged instances apart afterwards.
import.partialHint: Partial rather than failed: some entities came across and some did not. What did not is listed above.
import.pausedHint: Imported monitors are paused. Review them, then resume them from the monitor list.
import.resumeHint: Off by default: imported monitors arrive paused so you can review them before several thousand checks fire at once.
import.state.partial: Some things did not come across

incidents.affectedHint: Optional. Naming them is what lets a status page show which services are involved.
incidents.autoOpenedHint: Opened automatically by a monitor going down.
incidents.deleteConfirm: Delete this incident and its whole timeline? Anyone reading a status page will lose the record of it.
incidents.emptyHint: Incidents opened automatically by a monitor going down, or by hand, appear here.
incidents.firstUpdateHint: The sentence that explains what is happening. Required, because an incident with no words is one nobody can act on.
incidents.impactHint: How badly this affects the people using the service. `none` is still a real incident — a partner API degrading is worth recording.
incidents.notifyHint: Sends this update to the confirmed subscribers of every page above.
incidents.onPagesHint: Subscribers to these pages are told when an update says to.
incidents.startedAtHint: Defaults to now. Backdate it when the outage began before anyone noticed.
incidents.stateChangeNote: An incident advances through its timeline, so every state change carries the note explaining it.
incidents.subscriberDeliveryOff: This install cannot reach subscribers: it has no mail relay or no base URL configured, so an update marked “tell subscribers” will be recorded as suppressed. Settings has both.
incidents.title: Incident
incidents.titleHint: What a customer reading the status page will see first.
monitor.certificateNone: No certificate has been observed for this monitor.
monitor.probeHint: Which probe checks this. A Docker monitor asks a question only one host can answer, so it has to name one.
monitor.subtitle: {type} monitor for
monitors.confirmDelete: Delete {name}? Its history is deleted with it, and this cannot be undone.
monitors.emptyHint: Create your first monitor to start collecting heartbeats.
monitors.title: Monitors
overview.title: Dashboard
public.notFound: No status page exists at this address.
public.subscribeFailed: The subscription could not be recorded.
public.subscribeSent: Check your inbox. We have sent a confirmation link, and the subscription starts once you follow it.
reports.comparisonHint: The previous period is the same length placed immediately before, not the previous calendar period — 28 days beside 31 would make every count differ for calendar reasons.
reports.deleteHint: Every report it produced is kept. A run outlives the definition that made it.
reports.emptyHint: A template says what to report on and over what window. Schedules and runs come after it.
reports.maintenanceHint: The same window yields three different lawful percentages, so whichever you choose is printed on the report.
reports.name: Name
reports.responseTargetHint: Classifies days after the fact. Distinct from the monitor's own threshold, which marks a check down.
reports.scopeHint: Resolved when the report runs, not when you save it. Add a monitor to a tag and it is in the next report.
reports.slaTargetHint: Overrides the monitors' own. Below 100: a target of exactly 100 has an error budget of zero seconds.
reports.title: Reports
reports.typeHint.comparative: Two or more series side by side.
reports.typeHint.custom: Every block, with sections choosing which appear.
reports.typeHint.post_mortem: The incident log, with time to detect, acknowledge and resolve.
reports.typeHint.sla: Target versus actual, error budget consumed and remaining, burn rate, and a breach log.
reports.typeHint.uptime: The default. No SLO vocabulary anywhere on it, even where the monitors have targets.
runs.emptyHint: Generate a report from a template, or wait for a schedule to fire.
runs.expiredHint: The bytes were reclaimed by retention. The record of what was sent is kept.
runs.lateHint: This run started more than fifteen minutes after it was due.
runs.mirrorFailedHint: The report itself is fine and downloadable. Only the offsite copy failed.
runs.noDeliveries: Not scheduled, so nobody was sent it
runs.partialHint: One format was produced and another was not. The files that rendered are below.
runs.shareHint: Anyone with the link can read this report. It is not indexed by search engines and can be revoked at any time.
runs.shareOnce: Copy this now. It is shown once and cannot be read back.
runs.unavailableHint: This report was produced but its file is not in the reports directory. The usual cause is a database restored without the reports directory; its digest and size are still recorded, so the file can be identified in a backup.
settings.baseUrlHint: The public URL of this install. Every alert link, push URL, and subscriber link is built from it — leave it empty and alerts arrive without one.
settings.instanceNameHint: Shown in authenticator apps and on status pages.
settings.mirrorBucketWarning: The bucket must not be public. A public bucket holding client reports is a data breach with no code defect behind it. Do not put your encryption key in the same bucket as a database backup.
settings.mirrorEncryptionHint: Passed through to the provider. Artifacts are not encrypted before upload: monitor names and uptime figures are already plaintext in the database.
settings.mirrorEndpointHint: Leave empty for AWS. Set it for MinIO, R2, Backblaze, Garage or Ceph.
settings.mirrorHint: An optional offsite copy of every rendered report, to an S3-compatible bucket. Local storage under the data directory stays the source of truth and the only read path, so a failed upload is recorded against the artifact rather than failing the report. This is not the same as a schedule's S3 delivery, which drops one run's files for a recipient.
settings.mirrorPathStyleHint: Puts the bucket in the path rather than the hostname. MinIO, Garage and Ceph commonly need this; AWS prefers the alternative.
settings.mirrorRegionHint: Required for the request signature even where your provider ignores it. If you are unsure, us-east-1 is the conventional answer for S3-compatible servers.
settings.mirrorSecretStored: A secret is stored. Leave empty to keep it — it is encrypted at rest and never read back.
settings.mirrorSecretUnset: No secret stored yet. It is encrypted at rest and never read back.
settings.monitoringHint: What a newly created monitor inherits. Changing these does not touch monitors that already exist.
settings.reportArtifactDaysHint: How long a rendered report's bytes are kept. Deliberately independent of the rollup tiers: a report is expected to outlive the data it was computed from. Zero keeps them forever. When they are reclaimed the record stays, so a shared link says the report existed rather than that it never did.
settings.retentionHint: Days kept per tier. Zero keeps it indefinitely, which on a Raspberry Pi is how the card fills up. Raw heartbeats are the expensive tier; the rollups above them are what every history range beyond a week is made of.
settings.smtpHint: The instance-wide relay. An email notification channel with “use the instance relay” set reads from here, and status page subscribers are only reachable at all once this and a base URL are set.
settings.smtpNotConfigured: No relay configured. Email notifications using the instance relay, and every status page subscription, are undeliverable until there is one.
settings.smtpPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the stored one. It is encrypted at rest and never read back.
settings.telemetryHint: Off by default and off unless you turn it on. Nothing leaves this install while it is off.
settings.title: Settings
settings.trustedProxiesHint: IPs or CIDRs allowed to set X-Forwarded-For. Empty means the header is believed nowhere. Naming your reverse proxy here is what lets /metrics tell a local scraper from the whole internet arriving through one.
setup.intro: This install has no accounts yet. The account you create here is an administrator, and this page closes once it exists.
setup.title: Create the first administrator
statusPages.confirmDelete: Delete {title}? The page and its subscriber list go with it. Monitors are unaffected.
statusPages.confirmRemoveSubscriber: Remove {target}? They stop receiving updates from this page.
statusPages.customCSSHint: Injected into the public page. Markup and javascript: URLs are refused rather than stripped — this is served to your visitors.
statusPages.customDomainHint: A hostname this page is served on. DNS and the certificate are yours to arrange at the reverse proxy — the deployment docs carry Caddy, nginx, and Traefik recipes.
statusPages.deleteHint: The page and everyone subscribed to it are removed. The monitors it lists are not touched.
statusPages.deliveryOff: Subscriber delivery is off on this install: it needs instance SMTP settings and general.base_url. Until both exist, a subscribe box would take an address nothing could write to.
statusPages.emptyHint: A status page is the public view of a set of monitors — pick which ones appear, group them into sections, and publish it on its own URL.
statusPages.name: Name
statusPages.noSections: No sections yet. A page with no sections shows visitors nothing.
statusPages.noSubscribers: Nobody has subscribed to this page.
statusPages.passwordEditHint: Leave blank to keep the current password. It is stored hashed and cannot be shown again.
statusPages.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. Visitors are asked for it before the page renders.
statusPages.publishedHint: An unpublished page is invisible on the public path, so it can be built before launch.
statusPages.searchFailed: The search could not be completed.
statusPages.sectionEmpty: No monitors in this section yet.
statusPages.sectionsHint: Ordered groupings of monitors as visitors see them. A monitor appears in at most one section.
statusPages.showPoweredByHint: Removable — nothing in the open source build is paywalled.
statusPages.slugEditHint: Changing this changes the public URL. Anything already linking to the old one stops working.
statusPages.slugHint: The public path this page is served on: /status/your-slug. Lower-case letters, digits, and hyphens.
statusPages.subscriptionsHint: A subscribe box on the public page. Every address is confirmed by email before anything is sent to it.
statusPages.timezoneHint: An IANA zone name such as Australia/Sydney. Blank uses UTC.
statusPages.unresolvedMonitor: This monitor could not be read.
statusPages.uptimeBarDaysHint: Days of history in the bar under each monitor, between 7 and 365.
subscription.confirmFailed: This confirmation link is no longer valid.
subscription.confirmFailedHint: It may already have been used, or the subscription may have been removed. Subscribing again will send a fresh link.
subscription.confirmed: You are subscribed. You will receive updates when an incident is opened, updated, or resolved.
subscription.unsubscribeFailed: This link is no longer valid.
subscription.unsubscribeFailedHint: You may already have unsubscribed. Either way, no further messages will be sent to this subscription.
subscription.unsubscribePrompt: Stop receiving status updates for this page?
subscription.unsubscribed: You have been unsubscribed. You will not receive any further updates.
taxonomy.confirmDeleteGroup: Delete {name}? Its monitors and any groups nested under it survive — they become ungrouped and top-level.
taxonomy.confirmDeleteTag: Delete {name}? It is removed from every monitor carrying it. The monitors themselves are untouched.
taxonomy.groupsHint: A monitor belongs to one group. A group reports the worst status among its monitors, including those in groups nested under it.
taxonomy.hasChildren: This group has groups nested under it, so it cannot itself be nested.
taxonomy.noGroups: No groups yet. Groups are for structure a monitor has exactly one of — a customer, a site, an environment.
taxonomy.noTags: No tags yet. A tag can be applied to a thousand monitors at once from the list.
taxonomy.parentHint: Groups nest one level deep in this release, so only top-level groups can be a parent.
taxonomy.slugHint: A URL-safe slug is derived from the name by the server. It needs at least one ASCII letter or digit.
taxonomy.slugIs: URL slug: {slug}. It follows the name, so renaming changes it.
taxonomy.tagsHint: A monitor carries any number of tags. Use them for the things that cut across groups — priority, owner, region.
